sam: heads up — int4 bring-up (qwenx -> mistralx) showing progressive quality drift after ~2k tokens, seems deterministic across runs. repro script + model convert used below. attaching short sample outputs.

sam: repro command:
```bash
./convert_model --src qwenx-7b-int4.bin --dst mistralx-7b-q4.bin --embed-stride 1 --head-stride 1 --quant int4
python eval_longcontext.py --model mistralx-7b-q4.bin --prompt-file tests/long_context_prompts.txt --max-tokens 4096
```

sam: example diff (truncated):
- expected: "...the recommendation is to use the cached KV..."
- actual:   "...the recommendatio is t use the cacheKV..."

mia: interesting. does this look like tokenizer drift or an embed/head layout issue? can you paste the tokenizer hash and vocab len? @sam

sam: tokenizer: qwenx-tokenizer v1 (sha256: 3f2b...) vocab_len=50288
sam: conversion log shows no errors, but converter prints: "WARN: embed interleaver detected non-uniform stride, applying heuristic mapping"

jun: "embed interleaver" + "heuristic mapping" is sounding like the culprit. we've seen off-by-one embed strides break rotary indexing before. can you run with --embed-stride 2 (force even) and compare? also try --kv-offset 0/1 to see KV cache alignment effects.

sam: ran quick runs. results:
- embed-stride=1, kv-offset=0 -> perf drop, hallucinations at ~2100 tokens
- embed-stride=2, kv-offset=0 -> outputs align with baseline until 8k tokens (no drift) :thumbsup:
- embed-stride=1, kv-offset=1 -> partial improvement, still small token corruptions

liam: can you share a short eval table? even token-level edit distance or perplexities will help.

sam: quick numbers on 50 prompts (long context):
- baseline fp16 mistralx: ppl=12.4, tok_ed=0.012
- qwenx->mistralx int4 embed-stride=1: ppl=34.7, tok_ed=0.098
- qwenx->mistralx int4 embed-stride=2: ppl=13.1, tok_ed=0.015

karina: that delta is massive. sounds like converter chose an odd interleave layout for 1 which misaligned embedding vector lanes. probably affects rotary packing too. can you dump the first token embedding vectors (uint8/hex) pre/post conversion for a suspect token id?

sam: dumping now, attaching small hex blobs inline:
- src embed[1234] = 0x3f2a9d...
- dst embed[1234] = 0x9d3f2a... (pattern looks like a cyclic rotation)

mia: cyclic rotation -> definitely a lane reorder. check the converter code path that handles "embed_stride" in convert/kernels/pack.cpp — we changed pack order for some Qwen variants last quarter. maybe the heuristic assumed head-major layout.

jun: also confirm rotary angle alignment: if you permute embedding lanes without applying the same headwise rotary reshape, cos/sin multiply will be applied to wrong pairs. quick test: run the model with rotary disabled (fallback) — if drift disappears then it's rotary/head reshape mismatch.

sam: did that. rotary off -> outputs match baseline. rotary on + embed-stride=1 -> corruption.

ops-bot: ci/convert-smoke #842 failed on linux-amd64: converter unit test "embed_interleaver_roundtrip" assertion mismatch (expected equal, got rotated)

liam: can you produce a minimal failing unit test and open a draft PR? I can help with the kernel patch. also we should add an eval that runs a long-context generation smoke to catch regressions.

karina: checklist: 1) add roundtrip test that exercises odd embed_stride + rotary enabled; 2) fix pack order in converter (preserve lane ordering or document expected mapping); 3) add longcontext smoke in CI using a tiny prompt (1000 tokens) to catch drift; 4) verify tokenizer id mapping NFKC normalization isn't also shifting indices (unlikely but quick to check).

sam: creating PR now with failing test + small repro script. assigning to @liam and @jun for kernel and rotary sanity patch. will also add a quick eval in the nightly longcontext suite.

jun: if we need a hotfix for dedicated instances, we can ship a converter-compat patch that forces embed-stride=2 mapping for converted models until we have full fix. cc @ops-bot for release action.

ops-bot: release candidate "converter-hotfix-4995" created, canary scheduled to 3 hosts in ashburn on Tue 02:00 UTC.

sam: thanks — will attach logs and small failing prompt to the PR. adding labels: triage/priority-high, area/convert. :bug: :mag:

mia: nice catch. good call on the interleaver heuristic. once fixed, let's run the full quant-eval suite across qwen/mistral/gemma to ensure no other variants used the same pack assumptions.

liam: happy to pair on kernel change tomorrow. short-term guardrails in converter + CI longcontext should mitigate risk.

karina: adding e2e eval item to tracking board.

sam: closing loop — PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/convert/pull/2148 (draft)
